purpose: Synthetic event-level football data for detecting persistent tactical exposure while distinguishing it from isolated dangerous events and benign high-possession patterns.
important_notice: All teams, players, events, match dates, and labels are fictional and synthetically generated. This is not real Premier League data.

files.matches.csv: One row per fictional match. Each of 12 scenario archetypes has five variants with mixed match-level outcomes.
files.events.csv: Event-level observations. The two event flags reconcile dangerous turnovers and opponent attacking entries to each 15-minute window.
files.players.csv: Fictional roster with unique synthetic full names and positions.
files.match_windows.csv: Six 15-minute aggregates per match. Count and average fields are reconciled to events.csv.
files.ground_truth_labels.csv: Window-level synthetic persistent-risk and transient-spike labels. These are constructed benchmark targets, not universal tactical truth.
files.evaluation_cases.csv: Three distinct evaluation prompts per match. Expected answer criteria are for evaluation only and must not be model inputs.
files.data_dictionary.json: Schema, provenance, definitions, recommended evaluation, and limitations.

key_fields.x: Longitudinal coordinate from 0 to 100; for synthetic analysis, higher values represent closer to the opponent goal.
key_fields.y: Lateral coordinate from 0 to 100; higher values correspond to the right channel from the attacking team's perspective in this simplified convention.
key_fields.defenders_behind_ball: Synthetic count of players behind the ball at the event time.
key_fields.recovery_speed_index: Synthetic normalized index between 0 and 1; higher means faster recovery.
key_fields.fatigue_index: Synthetic normalized proxy between 0 and 1; not a physiological measurement.
key_fields.expert_persistent_risk_label: Synthetic ground-truth label for sustained exposure at the window level.
key_fields.expert_transient_spike_label: Synthetic label for a dangerous isolated spike that should not alone trigger a persistent-risk alert.
key_fields.scenario_type: Tactical setup archetype. Each archetype contains both positive and negative match variants; it is not a proxy for the target label.
key_fields.is_dangerous_turnover: Binary event flag set on a subject-team turnover judged to create immediate transition danger. Its window sum equals dangerous_turnovers_observed.
key_fields.is_attacking_entry: Binary event flag set when the opponent enters the attacking third. Its window sum equals opponent_attacking_entries.
key_fields.evaluation_focus: One of three evaluation tasks: risk assessment, spike-versus-pattern distinction, or tactical adjustment.
key_fields.expert_risk_intensity: Synthetic 0-1 indicator computed from turnover danger, opponent entries, recovery, and defensive cover. It is not a calibrated probability.

recommended_validation: Use a grouped split by scenario_type when evaluating transfer to unseen tactical archetypes. At minimum, keep all windows from a match_id in one split.
Exclude scenario_type, scenario_title, scenario_description, ground-truth labels, evaluation prompts and criteria, IDs, and generator metadata from model inputs.
Compare a turnover-count baseline with models that use dangerous-turnover counts, opponent entries, recovery, defensive cover, and temporal persistence.
Report precision, recall, F1, false-alert rate, and calibration at match and window levels. Do not treat windows as independent when estimating uncertainty.
Evaluate false_alarm, single_event_noise, recovery_success, and chaotic_endgame separately.
Use deterministic calculations for metrics. Use an LLM to explain validated findings rather than invent numeric facts.
limitations: All teams, player names, matches, events, scores, scenarios, and labels are fictional and synthetic.
The 48 expanded matches are controlled perturbations of 12 seed archetypes. They increase variation for prototyping but do not provide 60 independent real-world observations.
Labels are constructed to test persistence, false alarms, and transient spikes. They are not universal tactical truth or evidence of real-world performance.
Pitch coordinates, pressure, recovery speed, fatigue, defensive cover, and event flags are simplified synthetic measures, not calibrated tracking data.
A grouped split by scenario_type is still a small synthetic benchmark and cannot establish real-world generalization.
